50.7 THE INVARIANT

13. Across the entire executed matrix, the count of rows with `eclipse_verdict = ROBUST` and `block_miss = 1` must be exactly zero. This is a build gate, not a metric. If it is ever nonzero: stop, do not publish, write the counterexample cell to `bench/results/<run_id>/VIOLATIONS.json` with the bundle hash, seed, operator and certificate, add it as a regression fixture, and fix the kernel.
14. A row with any flag set (`grounding_capped`, `subset_minimal_only`, `greedy_cover`) may never carry verdict `ROBUST`. Assert it in the runner, in the Rust kernel, and in the Go checker independently. Three independent assertions, because this is the one claim the whole artifact rests on.
15. Also assert: `cut_size >= lower_bound`; `corridors_min <= corridors_max`; `Reach(P_min) ⊆ Reach(P_max)` sampled per cell; `checker_ok = true` for every non-CRASH row; and certificate re-verification offline from `certs/` reproduces the same verdict byte-for-byte.

```bash
#    hardware; scales roughly linearly with core count
```

51.4 THREATS TO VALIDITY

Write section 15 with these five subsections, each with concrete named threats and the mitigation actually implemented:

6. **Construct validity.** The metrics may not measure security value. The 60-second bucket matching is a choice; report sensitivity to bucket width {30,60,300}s. `actions_to_truth` uses a scripted analyst that no real analyst resembles.
7. **Internal validity.** Ground truth is generator-declared, so SPECTRA and the generator share a world model; a rule table and a generator authored by the same person can agree by construction. Mitigation: the rule table is written against source schemas, not against scenario scripts; a held-out scenario set (`S80..S85`) is authored after the rule table is frozen, and its results are reported separately. State whether held-out performance dropped. It probably did; that is the finding.
8. **External validity.** All telemetry is synthetic. No claim transfers to production data. Volumes, entity cardinalities and noise distributions are declared in the manifest and are not calibrated against any real environment, because no real environment was available.
9. **Statistical validity.** Seeds are not independent across operators applied to the same base scenario; pairing handles the mean but not all dependence. Bootstrap assumes exchangeability across seeds. Family sizes for Holm correction are stated per metric.
10. **Attacker model validity.** The attacker is non-adaptive and does not observe the control configuration. A control cut that severs this attacker's chain says nothing about an attacker who adapts to the cut. Say this in the abstract, not only here.
11. Each subsection ends with a line of the form `Unmitigated: <list>`. An empty `Unmitigated:` line is not credible and CI rejects it.

13. Forbidden edits: removing an RQ after seeing results; renaming a metric so an unfavourable comparison disappears; adding a post-hoc filter that excludes inconvenient scenarios; reporting the best of several runs. If a run is discarded, record why in `bench/results/INDEX.json` under `discarded[]` with a reason string; discarded runs are never deleted.

============================================================
52. BUILD ORDER AND MILESTONES
============================================================

52.1 Rules of sequencing

1. Milestones are strictly ordered M0 -> M10. **Do not start a milestone until the previous one is green.** "Green" means: its `make` proof target exits 0 on a clean clone, in CI, twice in a row, with no manual step.
2. Every milestone ends with a single command, `make mN-verify`, that prints a machine-parsable block and exits non-zero on any failure. No milestone is "done by inspection".
3. Every milestone adds a row to `docs/STATUS.md` generated by `make status` from the actual CI artifacts. Never hand-edit that file.
4. A thin vertical slice (generate -> ingest -> reconstruct -> replay -> visible in UI) must exist at **M3**. Nothing after M3 may break the slice; `make demo-slice` runs in every subsequent milestone's verify target.
5. The polyglot long tail (section 19) begins only at **M9**. Do not scatter languages across M0-M8 to look productive. Languages added before M9 are only those the core genuinely needs: Python, Rust, Go, TypeScript, SQL, Bash, Dockerfile, YAML, TOML, Makefile, plus Haskell at M6 (differential oracle) and C at M4 if and only if the liveness hot loop demonstrably needs it with a benchmark to prove it.
6. If a milestone cannot be completed as specified, stop and report per section 56. Do not silently redefine the acceptance criteria.

52.2 Milestone table

| ID  | Name                          | Proof target            | New languages                | Slice state |
|-----|-------------------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------|-------------|
| M0  | Skeleton and toolchain        | `make m0-verify`        | Bash, Make, Docker, YAML, TOML | none |
| M1  | Generator and ground truth    | `make m1-verify`        | Python                       | none |
| M2  | Ingest, ER, event store       | `make m2-verify`        | SQL, Python                  | none |
| M3  | VERTICAL SLICE                | `make demo-slice`       | Rust, TypeScript, Go         | alive |
| M4  | Liveness, licenses, fixpoint  | `make m4-verify`        | (C only if benchmarked)      | alive |
| M5  | Two-sided cut + certificate   | `make m5-verify`        | -                            | alive |
| M6  | Independent checker + gates   | `make m6-verify`        | Haskell                      | alive |
| M7  | Degradation and tampering     | `make m7-verify`        | R or Julia (analysis only)   | alive |
| M8  | Full UI and PROVE flow        | `make m8-verify`        | CSS/SCSS, HTML               | alive |
| M9  | Polyglot surface + perf       | `make m9-verify`        | the remaining target set     | alive |
| M10 | Docs, demo, release           | `make release-check`    | -                            | alive |

```
M0 ─ M1 ─ M2 ─ M3 ══════════════ vertical slice frozen ══════════════▶
                │
                └─ M4 ─ M5 ─ M6 ─ M7 ─ M8 ─ M9 ─ M10
                   \_____ ECLIPSE kernel _____/   \_ surface _/
```

52.3 M0 — Skeleton and toolchain

- Goal: a clone of the repo builds, lints and tests an empty system, offline, on Linux/macOS/WSL2.
- Deliverables: directory tree per section 8; `docker-compose.yml` (postgres, redis, api, web, worker) with pinned digests; `Makefile` with the full target vocabulary; `.tool-versions`/`rust-toolchain.toml`/`go.mod`/`package.json` with exact pins; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `.editorconfig`; pre-commit hooks; `make bootstrap` that installs nothing outside the repo and container images.
- Acceptance: `docker compose up -d` reaches healthy for all services in < 90s; `make lint test build` exits 0 with zero test cases skipped; CI runs with `--network=none` for the test job and passes; `git clean -xdf && make bootstrap && make m0-verify` passes on a second machine profile in CI matrix.
- Proof: `make m0-verify` prints versions of every toolchain, the compose health table, and `M0 OK`.
- Demo capability: none. This milestone unlocks nothing user-visible and must not be presented as progress on the product.

52.4 M1 — Generator and ground truth

- Goal: seeded synthetic telemetry with recorded ground truth, honestly generated.
- Deliverables: `spectra-gen` CLI; scenario definitions in `scenarios/*.toml`; at least 6 scenarios covering identity, session, credential, privilege, process, network, service-account and trust dimensions; ground-truth file `truth.json` recording the true attack step sequence and true control dependencies; manifest with BLAKE3 hash and seed; per-source sequence chaining (used later by liveness).
- Acceptance: identical seed produces byte-identical `bundle.jsonl` and identical manifest hash across 3 runs and across Linux/macOS; `truth.json` is never read by any ingest, reconstruction or kernel code — enforced by a build-time import/dependency test and a grep gate in CI; generator emits volume/timing statistics that are computed, not declared.
- Proof: `make m1-verify` (hash triple-run equality, truth-isolation gate, scenario schema validation).
- Demo capability: `spectra gen --scenario s1 --seed 7` produces a dataset you can show on screen. Nothing more.

52.5 M2 — Ingest, entity resolution, event store

- Goal: heterogeneous records become entity-resolved, time-indexed, stable-ID events in Postgres.
- Deliverables: parsers per source type; normalization to the canonical event schema (section 12); entity resolution with deterministic tie-breaking; `EventId` assignment stable across re-ingest; SQL DDL and migrations; `spectra ingest`.
- Acceptance: re-ingesting the same bundle yields the identical `EventId` set (`SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE event_id NOT IN (...)` = 0); ER precision/recall measured against `truth.json` **only in the evaluation harness**, reported as numbers from a real run; ingest of a 2M-record bundle completes within the documented budget and the measured number is written to `bench/ingest.json`; no `NOW()`, no random UUIDs, no wall-clock in any ID derivation (lint rule `no-nondeterminism` passes).
- Proof: `make m2-verify`.
- Demo capability: query the event store, show entity clusters. Still no product story.

52.6 M3 — VERTICAL SLICE (mandatory earliest end-to-end)

- Goal: one command takes a scenario from generation to a replayed control configuration rendered in the browser.
- Deliverables: (a) deterministic reconstruction producing the state-transition timeline and the causal graph; (b) `rules.toml` v1 with at least 25 rules compiled to Rust; (c) the concrete control simulator driven by the **same guard AST** as the future kernel (section on CCL); (d) `POST /api/replay` accepting a control configuration and returning the deterministic outcome; (e) React view: timeline, causal graph, control toggle panel, outcome banner.
- Acceptance:
  - `make demo-slice` runs headless end to end in < 3 minutes and asserts on real output, not on exit codes alone.
  - Toggling `session_binding` from 0 to 1 in the API changes the terminal node of the attack path, and the changed node is asserted by test, not screenshotted.
  - Two identical replay requests return byte-identical JSON including ordering of arrays.
  - The UI renders the same terminal node as the API returns (Playwright test compares DOM text to API JSON).
  - Removing the LLM service from compose changes nothing: `make demo-slice NO_LLM=1` passes with identical outputs except narration fields, which must be absent, not empty-stringed.
- Proof: `make demo-slice` plus `make m3-verify` (which runs demo-slice + determinism + no-LLM run).
- Demo capability: **the product exists.** You can show: here is the attack, here is the state reconstruction, flip this control, the chain dies at step 4. Every claim on screen traces to real computation.

52.7 M4 — Liveness, licenses, silent envelope, fixpoint

- Goal: ECLIPSE pipeline stages A-D.
- Deliverables: per-source liveness with BLAKE3 chain checks and q99 inter-arrival from this run's own data; `liveness.json`; Bellman-Ford difference-constraint pass voiding backdated licenses; semi-naive grounding with provenance producing the AND/OR hypergraph; silent instance generation gated on `∀s ∈ producing_sources(τ): ¬live(s,I)`; the ~40 obligation axioms, each with a must-fire and a must-not-fire unit test; `P_min` and `P_max`; Dowling-Gallier fixpoint under a cut mask.
- Acceptance: all 40 obligation axioms have both tests and both pass; grounding sizes are measured and written to `bench/grounding.json` with caps recorded; a rule-ordering property test (≥ 500 randomized orderings) yields byte-identical fixpoints; `Reach(P_min) ⊆ Reach(P_max)` asserted on every fixture; the delete-effect linter rejects a deliberately malformed rule in a negative test; ghost (silent) instances never appear in any observed-event count — asserted by a test that counts both.
- Proof: `make m4-verify`.
- Demo capability: show blind windows per source on the timeline and the GHOST-rendered hypothetical steps, clearly marked as permissions, not observations.

52.8 M5 — Two-sided minimal cut and certificate

- Goal: ECLIPSE stages E and the certificate object.
- Deliverables: Reiter/MARCO hitting-set loop over clause DB Ψ; minimum-cardinality model by popcount-ordered branch and bound over `u64` masks; threshold-literal implications `x_{k,ℓ+1} → x_{k,ℓ}` enforced; witness-tree extraction; `S_opt` on `P_min`, `S_rob` on `P_max`; corridor sets `Ψ_min`, `Ψ_max`; blindness premium `S_rob \ S_opt` with the responsible licenses named; certificate serialization exactly as specified in section on ECLIPSE, content-addressed by BLAKE3; downgrade to subset-minimal with the `subset_minimal_only` flag when `|A| > 64`.
- Acceptance: on every fixture, an exhaustive brute-force over all cuts (fixtures sized so this is feasible, `|A| ≤ 18`) confirms `|S_opt|` and `|S_rob|` are truly minimum; the antitonicity test over the control lattice passes (raising any level never re-enables the goal); a flagged run (capped grounding, greedy cover, or subset-minimal) can never carry `mode: ROBUST` — negative test asserts the builder refuses; blindness premium is non-empty on at least two fixtures and each element names ≥ 1 license.
- Proof: `make m5-verify`.
- Demo capability: PROVE returns a real certificate hash and a real minimum cut.

52.9 M6 — Independent Go checker and differential gates

- Goal: the certificate is verifiable by code that shares nothing with the solver.
- Deliverables: `spectra verify` as a separate Go module under `checker/` with its own `go.mod`, no dependency edge to the Rust workspace (enforced by a CI dependency-graph test); it re-grounds from hashed inputs and checks (a)-(f) per the ECLIPSE spec; a Haskell reference admissibility checker for license logic used as a differential oracle; the concrete-simulator-vs-kernel agreement gate over 256 randomized control configurations per fixture; Z3 as a test-only oracle, never a runtime dependency.
- Acceptance: `spectra verify` returns OK on all valid certificates in < 50ms for a 2k-instance scenario, measured and recorded; a mutation suite of ≥ 30 corrupted certificates (flipped cut atom, forged license, tampered bundle hash, truncated Ψ, wrong invariant `U`, witness leaf that is not a real `EventId`) each produce a distinct, specific failure and a non-zero exit; Rust-kernel vs Go-checker vs Haskell-oracle disagreement on any fixture fails the build; `grep -r` proves the checker links no Rust artifact and no shared crate.
- Proof: `make m6-verify`.
- Demo capability: the terminal pane in the demo that independently validates the proof in front of the viewer.

52.10 M7 — Degradation, tampering, redundancy, observation set, frontier

- Goal: the second research axis and ECLIPSE stages F, G, H.
- Deliverables: degradation matrix from 100% to 30% completeness in 10-point steps, crossed with the six perturbation modes (deletion, delay, duplication, reordering, corruption, targeted suppression), ≥ 20 seeds per cell; redundancy index `red(i,j)` from Ψ; decisive observation set (exact ≤ 3, greedy beyond with the `ln n + 1` bound printed and the `greedy_cover` flag set); multiple-choice knapsack frontier over declared costs; results serialized to `results/*.json` and rendered by the analysis language (R or Julia) into `docs/RESULTS.md` figures.
- Acceptance: **the invariant — zero false ROBUST verdicts across the entire matrix**, checked against generator ground truth, is asserted and the count printed; every published number is regenerated by `make bench` from scratch, and `make docs-check` fails if any number in `RESULTS.md` differs from `results/*.json`; costs come only from `costs.toml` and the test suite includes a case with no `costs.toml` where the frontier is expressed in control counts and says so; no probability, confidence score or dollar figure appears anywhere in output — enforced by a lexical gate on the JSON schemas and a CI grep over rendered docs.
- Proof: `make m7-verify` (runs the matrix at reduced seed count in CI, full matrix in `make bench`).
- Demo capability: the stability strip and the "which single log source collapses the ambiguity" beat.

52.11 M8 — Full UI and PROVE flow

- Goal: the flagship interaction, complete.
- Deliverables: control panel with per-control **levels** (not booleans); PROVE button; certificate header with mode, cut, corridor count and hash; counterexample derivation tree with real `EventId` leaves, expandable to the raw event record; blindness-premium panel naming licenses and their windows; GHOST styling for silent instances with a legend; embedded checker pane streaming real `spectra verify` output; stability strip; flag badges that are impossible to hide.
- Acceptance: Playwright suite asserts every on-screen number against the API response; a test asserts that a flagged run renders the flag badge and that `ROBUST` is not rendered; colour and GHOST distinction pass a contrast check; the UI works with the LLM service absent (narration panel renders an explicit "narration unavailable" state, never fabricated text); zero client-side computation of any verdict — a test greps the bundle for forbidden solver symbols.
- Proof: `make m8-verify`.
- Demo capability: the full 10-minute demo of section 54 can be performed by hand.

52.12 M9 — Polyglot surface and performance

- Goal: the remaining languages, each with a stated technical reason, plus measured performance.
- Deliverables: per section 19, each additional language ships as a real component with a justification line in `POLYGLOT.md`, its own tests, and a place on a code path or a documented offline workflow (e.g. YARA for artifact-pattern fixtures, Verilog/VHDL for the hardware-attestation sensor model, Solidity for the append-only evidence-anchor experiment, WebAssembly for the in-browser fixpoint replayer, Assembly for the BLAKE3 chain inner loop with a benchmark against the portable version, MATLAB/R/Julia for analysis, Swift/Kotlin/ObjC/Dart for platform telemetry collectors).
- Acceptance: every language in the target list either (a) has a component, a test and a justification, or (b) is explicitly listed in `POLYGLOT.md` as not used, with the reason. **No language may exist solely as a hello-world or a re-implementation of an existing CRUD path** — a reviewer checklist item and a CI check that each language directory contains at least one test that fails when its source is mutated. Performance numbers for the Assembly/C paths must include the portable baseline; if the optimized path is not faster, say so and keep the baseline as default.
- Proof: `make m9-verify` + `make polyglot-report`.
- Demo capability: a credible repository language surface backed by real code.

52.13 M10 — Documentation, demo, release

- Goal: the repository is presentable and the demo cannot rot.
- Deliverables: every document in section 53; the recorded assets of section 54; the GitHub surface of section 55; `v0.1.0` tag and release notes; `make demo` non-interactive; `make release-check` running the union of all `mN-verify` targets plus docs checks.
- Acceptance: `make release-check` green from a clean clone with no network beyond image pulls; every README claim maps to a passing test or a command in the demo transcript; `docs-check` confirms no number in docs is unbacked; `LIMITATIONS.md` contains every item from the ECLIPSE "may never claim" list verbatim in substance.
- Proof: `make release-check`.
- Demo capability: a stranger can clone and reproduce the demo in 10 minutes.

============================================================
53. DOCUMENTATION SET
============================================================

53.1 Required tree

```
README.md            SECURITY.md          CITATION.cff
CHANGELOG.md         CONTRIBUTING.md      CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
LICENSE              docs/
  ARCHITECTURE.md      RULES.md        BENCHMARK.md   DEMO.md
  SECURITY-MODEL.md    CONTROLS.md     RESULTS.md     DEVELOPMENT.md
  THREAT-MODEL.md      SCENARIOS.md    LIMITATIONS.md STATUS.md      (generated)
  STATE-MODEL.md       METHODOLOGY.md  DATASETS.md    POLYGLOT.md
  ECLIPSE.md           RESEARCH.md     adr/0000-template.md
  adr/NNNN-<slug>.md
```

53.2 README.md — exact section order

1. Project name, one-sentence definition, status banner.
2. **Status/maturity banner**, verbatim shape: `> Status: research prototype (v0.1.0, milestone M10). Synthetic data only. Not a security product. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md.`
3. Hero asset (see 53.3).
4. What SPECTRA does — five bullets, each naming the deterministic mechanism that produces it.
5. **What this is not** — explicit list: not a SIEM/SOC/EDR, not a vulnerability or CVE scanner, not an SBOM or dependency tool, not a malware analyzer, not a CSPM, not a phishing detector, not an LLM wrapper, not formal verification of any real system, not a supply-chain tool (that is the author's other project, WARDEN, linked, with the one-line distinction).
6. Quickstart: `git clone`, `make bootstrap`, `make demo` — exactly the commands of section 54, no others.
7. The flagship: control replay and ECLIPSE, with the certificate example and the real checker transcript.
8. How it works — 12-line ASCII pipeline diagram, each stage linking to its doc.
9. Reproducibility: seeds, pinned versions, hashes, `make bench`.
10. Results summary — at most 4 numbers, each with the command that regenerates it.
11. Repository layout and language map (link to POLYGLOT.md).
12. Limitations (3 lines + link).
13. Citation, license, acknowledgements.

53.3 Hero asset requirements

The hero must show, in one loop under 20 seconds, the causal graph with a control panel, a PROVE press, the certificate header line with a real hash, one control untoggled, and the counterexample tree lighting with real event IDs. It must be generated by `make demo-assets` from a real run. A hero that is a logo, a stock illustration, or a hand-drawn mockup is forbidden.

53.4 README rules (hard)

- No fabricated stars, downloads, "used by", or contributor counts.
- Badge set restricted per section 55.5. No vanity badges.
- Every feature stated in the README must be reachable by a command in `DEMO.md` or covered by a named test; `make docs-check` maps README claim anchors to test IDs listed in `docs/claims.toml` and fails on an unmapped claim.
- No roadmap items written in the present tense. Unbuilt things live in `ROADMAP` sections marked `planned, not implemented`.
- No screenshots of states the code cannot produce.

53.5 Per-document contents

| Document | Must contain |
|---|---|
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | Component diagram; process/container boundaries; data flow from bundle to certificate; language-per-component table with the reason; sync/async boundaries; storage schema overview; failure modes; what is deterministic and where the only nondeterminism (none in the core) could enter |
| `SECURITY-MODEL.md` | What SPECTRA models: the ten state dimensions, the control catalog semantics, control **levels**, guard AST, the monotonicity argument, why time-indexing replaces retraction, the exact meaning of ROBUST / OPTIMISTIC-ONLY / UNSAFE |
| `THREAT-MODEL.md` | Threats to the platform itself (malicious bundle, hostile rules file, adversarial suppression, resource exhaustion during grounding); trust boundaries; the non-adaptive-attacker assumption stated plainly; explicitly: SPECTRA is not hardened for untrusted multi-tenant input |
| `STATE-MODEL.md` | Per-dimension state machines as ASCII diagrams; transition tables; entity-resolution rules; identity of a state over time; worked example with real event IDs |
| `RULES.md` | The full rule table rendered from `rules.toml`; for each rule: head, body, guard, `producing_sources`, `silent_possible`, provenance note, the two unit tests; the 40 obligation axioms; the delete-effect prohibition |
| `CONTROLS.md` | Control catalog with ordered levels `L_k`, threshold literal encoding, implication chain, which rules each level blocks, and the statement that costs are user input only |
| `SCENARIOS.md` | Each scenario: narrative, entities, timeline, ground-truth attack steps, expected cut, expected blindness premium, the seed |
| `METHODOLOGY.md` | How every measurement is produced: fixtures, seeds, repetitions, hardware, what is excluded, how ground truth is used only in evaluation; the false-ROBUST invariant and how it is checked |
| `RESEARCH.md` | The two research questions; related work with citations; where SPECTRA differs; what would falsify the claims; open problems |
| `BENCHMARK.md` | Benchmark harness, commands, hardware, warm-up policy, variance reporting (min/median/max over n runs, never a single number) |
| `RESULTS.md` | Generated from `results/*.json` by `make docs-figures`; degradation matrix, corridor counts, cut sizes, checker latency, grounding sizes; every figure captioned with the generating command and input hash |
| `LIMITATIONS.md` | The complete ECLIPSE "may never claim" list; model-relative soundness; unmodeled techniques; synthetic-data caveat; no probabilities; capped-grounding and greedy-cover flags; perfectly suppressed events are permanently invisible and the per-dimension blind-spot volume is published instead |
| `DATASETS.md` | Generator design, distributions, seeds, manifest hashes, size table, how to regenerate, why no real data is used, how to add a scenario |
| `POLYGLOT.md` | Table of language -> component -> why this language -> tests -> lines; an explicit "not used and why" list |
| `DEVELOPMENT.md` | Setup, make target vocabulary, test layers, how to add a rule/control/scenario/language, lint rules including `no-nondeterminism`, commit conventions, how to run the differential gates locally |
| `DEMO.md` | The section 54 script verbatim, with copy-pasteable commands and expected output excerpts |
| `SECURITY.md` | Reporting channel, scope (this is research software; no production use), no bounty, response expectations |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Issue and PR flow, the anti-slop checklist link, the rule that no PR may add a number to docs without the generating command |
| `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` | Contributor Covenant 2.1, unmodified, with a real contact address |
| `LICENSE` | Single OSI license (Apache-2.0), matching `CITATION.cff` and package metadata |
| `CITATION.cff` | Valid CFF 1.2.0, validated in CI |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | Keep a Changelog format, one entry per release, linked to tags |

53.6 CITATION.cff skeleton

```yaml
cff-version: 1.2.0
message: "If you use SPECTRA, please cite it."
title: "SPECTRA: Security State Reconstruction, Causal Analysis and Attack Replay"
version: 0.1.0
date-released: 2026-01-01
license: Apache-2.0
repository-code: "https://github.com/<user>/spectra"
abstract: >
  A deterministic, offline research platform that reconstructs security state
  from synthetic telemetry, emits evidence-licensed cut proofs (ECLIPSE), and
  replays scenarios under alternative control configurations.
keywords: [security-state, causal-analysis, attack-replay, minimal-cut, provenance]
authors:
  - family-names: <Surname>
    given-names: <Given>
```

53.7 ADR template (`docs/adr/0000-template.md`)

```markdown
# ADR NNNN: <decision title>
Status: proposed | accepted | superseded by ADR-MMMM
Date: YYYY-MM-DD
Milestone: M<n>

## Context
What forced a decision. Constraints. What was measured.

## Options
1. <option> — cost, risk, what it would make impossible later.
2. ...

## Decision
The chosen option, stated as a rule the code must follow.

## Consequences
Positive, negative, and what must now be tested to keep this true.

## Verification
The test ID or make target that would fail if this decision were violated.
```

Mandatory ADRs: monotone time-indexed encoding instead of retraction; single guard AST shared by simulator and kernel; Go checker as an independent module; `|A| ≤ 64` u64 masks and the subset-minimal downgrade; two fixpoints instead of world enumeration; exclusion of probabilities and Shapley values; BLAKE3 as the content-addressing function; Postgres as the event store.

============================================================
54. THE DEMO
============================================================

54.1 Constraints

- The demo runs from a **cold `git clone`** on a machine with Docker and no SPECTRA state.
- Total wall clock: 10 minutes, including builds, on the documented reference machine; the measured time is recorded in `docs/DEMO.md` and re-measured by CI monthly.
- Every number on screen is computed in that run. Nothing is pre-baked except container base images.
- `make demo` runs the entire path non-interactively and asserts on outputs, so the demo cannot rot.

54.2 Minute-by-minute script

```
T+0:00  $ git clone https://github.com/<user>/spectra && cd spectra
        $ make bootstrap
SCREEN  Image pulls, toolchain version table, "bootstrap OK (pinned)".
SAY     Everything is local and offline after this point.

T+1:00  $ make up
SCREEN  compose health table: postgres, redis, api, worker, web -> healthy.
        Browser opens http://localhost:5173 showing an empty workspace with
        the status banner "research prototype - synthetic data only".

T+1:30  $ spectra gen --scenario s3-contractor-token-pivot --seed 7
SCREEN  Generator prints source counts, time span, manifest:
          sources=9 records=418,220 span=14h03m
          bundle blake3:9c41e8...  seed=7
SAY     Seeded. Rerun it and you get the same bytes.

T+2:15  $ spectra ingest --bundle out/bundle.jsonl
SCREEN  Progress by source; then:
          events=418,220  entities=6,104  resolved_clusters=5,987
          stable EventIds assigned; re-ingest would be identical.

T+3:00  $ spectra reconstruct --run r1
SCREEN  UI switches to the timeline. Ten state dimensions as swimlanes.
        Causal graph appears; 6 blind windows shown as hatched bands on
        the iam_audit and edr lanes.
SAY     This is reconstruction, not detection. Nothing here is a score.

T+4:00  UI: open the Evidence drawer on node `priv.escalated@t=09:41:12`.
SCREEN  Three leaf EventIds with the raw records; provenance path to the
        rule instance that derived it, with the rule id and guard text.

T+4:45  UI: press PROVE (controls at their baseline levels).
SCREEN  Header:
          Minimum cut {session_binding>=bound, egress_seg>=1} - ROBUST
          6 corridors | |A|=23 | grounding 2,104 instances | blake3:3f9a...
        Right pane lists the two controls with their redundancy witnesses.

T+5:15  Terminal pane inside the UI runs the independent checker:
        $ spectra verify out/cert.json
          OK: closure verified (2104 instances), goal unreachable,
              2/2 witnesses valid, no cut of size 1 satisfies Psi. 11ms
SAY     Different language, different module, no shared code. It re-grounds
        from the hashes and checks the proof itself.

T+6:00  *** WOW MOMENT 1 - CONTROL REPLAY ***
        UI: set session_binding back to level 0. Press PROVE.
SCREEN  Banner flips to UNSAFE. The counterexample derivation tree animates
        open: 7 nodes, each leaf a real EventId, the terminal node is
        `data.exfil@t=11:58:40`. Checker pane: "goal REACHABLE - certificate
        is OPTIMISTIC-ONLY, not ROBUST".
SAY     The simulator and the proof kernel agree because they are generated
        from the same guard table. This is not a narrative; it is a derivation.

T+7:00  *** WOW MOMENT 2 - BLINDNESS PREMIUM ***
        UI: open the Blindness panel.
SCREEN  "credential_rotation is in the ROBUST cut ONLY because iam_audit was
         blind over [09:12:00, 09:52:00]. License L4 (basis: BLIND).
         Enabling iam_audit for those 40 minutes removes this control."
        Decisive observation set: {(iam_audit, [09:12,09:52])}, exact, size 1.
SAY     That is a control you are buying because you cannot see, not because
        the attacker needs it. GHOST steps are permissions, never observations.

T+8:00  $ make degrade SCENARIO=s3 SEEDS=5
SCREEN  Stability strip fills 100% -> 30% completeness. Cut stability, corridor
        counts, and the invariant line:
          false ROBUST verdicts: 0 / 350 cells
        Flags appear on the 40% and 30% cells: grounding_capped, greedy_cover.
SAY     Flagged runs can never print ROBUST. That is enforced in the builder.

T+9:00  UI: open the Frontier tab with costs.toml loaded.
SCREEN  Pareto points of (declared cost, residual reachability), each labelled
        with its cut and evidence IDs. A banner: "costs are user input".

T+9:30  $ make demo-verify
SCREEN  Re-runs the whole path headless and diffs against the run just shown:
          cert hash match, checker OK, 0 assertion failures. DEMO OK.
END     Close on docs/LIMITATIONS.md open on screen for 5 seconds.
```

54.3 `make demo` targets

```make
demo:          ## full non-interactive demo path, asserts on real output
	$(MAKE) bootstrap up
	spectra gen --scenario $(SCENARIO) --seed $(SEED) --out out/
	spectra ingest --bundle out/bundle.jsonl
	spectra reconstruct --run r1
	spectra prove --run r1 --mode robust --out out/cert.json
	spectra verify out/cert.json
	spectra prove --run r1 --controls session_binding=0 --out out/cert_unsafe.json
	python tools/assert_demo.py out/   # fails on any unexpected verdict/hash drift
	$(MAKE) degrade SCENARIO=$(SCENARIO) SEEDS=5
	@echo "DEMO OK"

demo-assets:   ## regenerate README media from a real run
demo-verify:   ## demo + diff against docs/DEMO.md expected excerpts
```

`make demo` runs in CI nightly and on every tag. A README asset older than its generating code (compared by input hash recorded in `assets/manifest.json`) fails `make docs-check`.

54.4 Recording plan

- Terminal: `asciinema rec --idle-time-limit 1.5 assets/casts/demo.cast` for each terminal segment; publish as `.cast` plus an SVG rendering; never edit the cast file by hand.
- Screen: 1920x1080, 30fps, no cursor trails, no personal data in the frame, system notifications off, browser in a clean profile with no extensions.
- Audio: none. Captions are burned-in text or none at all.
- Each asset records the commit SHA and input hashes in `assets/manifest.json`.

|---|---|---|---|
| `assets/hero.gif` | GIF, 20s loop | PROVE -> certificate header -> untoggle -> counterexample tree | 6 MB |
| `assets/replay.gif` | GIF, 12s | control levels changing the terminal node | 4 MB |

============================================================
55. REPOSITORY PRESENTATION
============================================================

55.1 Identity

- Description (<= 120 chars): `Deterministic security-state reconstruction, evidence-licensed cut proofs, and what-if control replay. Offline, synthetic data.`
- Topics: `security-research`, `causal-analysis`, `provenance`, `datalog`, `minimal-cut`, `attack-simulation`, `deterministic`, `rust`, `go`, `python`, `typescript`, `reproducible-research`, `offline-first`. No topic that is not true (`ai`, `agent`, `enterprise`, `production-ready` are forbidden).
- Social preview: generated from `assets/pipeline.svg` plus the project name and the status line. No stock imagery, no fake dashboards.
- Website field: link to the GitHub Pages docs build only if it exists; otherwise empty.

55.2 Issues, discussions, roadmap

- Pinned issues (exactly three): `ROADMAP: milestones M0-M10 and what is not built`, `LIMITATIONS: what SPECTRA does not and cannot claim`, `How to reproduce every number in the README`.
- Discussions enabled with categories: Q&A, Research, Show and tell. Seed exactly one Research post: the two research questions and what would falsify them.
- `ROADMAP.md` (or the pinned issue) marks every unbuilt item `planned, not implemented` with no date promises.
- Seed 5 `good first issue`s that are real and small: add a scenario, add an obligation axiom with its two tests, add a control level to `controls.toml`, add a language component from the POLYGLOT "not used" list, improve a figure caption. Each includes the exact files, the acceptance test, and the make target.

55.3 Templates

```
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml          # requires: commit SHA, make target, seed,
                                        #   bundle hash, full command, actual vs expected
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/rule_request.yml # requires: proposed rule, producing_sources,
                                        #   silent_possible, the must-fire/must-not-fire tests
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/research.yml     # requires: claim, how it could be falsified
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml       # blank_issues_enabled: false
.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
```

PR template checklist (all must be ticked, CI cross-checks the last four):

```
- [ ] Linked issue / ADR
- [ ] Determinism: reruns produce byte-identical output
- [ ] No number added to docs without its generating command
- [ ] New rule? both unit tests added (must-fire and must-not-fire)
- [ ] New control? levels, blocked rules, and lattice test added
- [ ] make lint test build demo-slice green locally
- [ ] Anti-slop checklist (section 56) run and pasted
```

55.4 Labels

`area/generator`, `area/ingest`, `area/kernel`, `area/checker`, `area/ui`, `area/docs`, `area/polyglot`, `type/bug`, `type/research`, `type/determinism`, `type/perf`, `good first issue`, `help wanted`, `blocked/milestone`, `wontfix/out-of-scope`. Labels are defined in `.github/labels.yml` and synced by CI.

55.5 Badges — allowed set only

Allowed, and only when the workflow actually exists and runs on `main`:

```
[CI] [determinism] [checker-differential] [degradation-invariant] [license] [release]
```

Forbidden: stars, forks, downloads, "made with love", "awesome", "production ready", "AI powered", code-quality letter grades, coverage badges unless coverage is genuinely measured and the number is real, any badge whose value is typed by hand into the README.

55.6 Releases

- Tag `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; `v0.x` until M10 is green.
- Release notes sections: `What works`, `What is proven by which gate`, `Known limitations`, `Reproduction` (exact commands + seeds + bundle hashes), `Changed since <prev>`, `Not implemented`.
- Attach: `cert.json` from the release run, `results/*.json`, the SBOM of the container images, the asciinema cast. No binaries that were not built by CI from the tagged commit.

55.7 Automation

- Dependabot for `cargo`, `gomod`, `npm`, `pip`, `docker`, `github-actions`, weekly, grouped, with a note in `CONTRIBUTING.md` that a dependency bump must keep hashes reproducible; a bump that changes any fixture hash must update the recorded hashes in the same PR with the regenerating command in the body.
- CODEOWNERS, branch protection on `main` requiring CI + `determinism` + `checker-differential`.
- No auto-merge for anything that touches `rules.toml`, `controls.toml`, the kernel, or the checker.

============================================================
56. FINAL ANTI-SLOP CHECKLIST AND REPORTING PROTOCOL
============================================================

56.1 Gate — run before declaring any milestone done

Run `make anti-slop`. It executes the following and prints a table. A single `FAIL` means the milestone is not done. Do not report a milestone as complete with a failing row and an explanation; fix it or report the milestone as incomplete.

```
 #  CHECK                                                       HOW IT IS PROVEN
 1  Clean-clone build green                                     git clean -xdf && make bootstrap build
 2  All tests green, zero skipped, zero xfail-without-issue     make test -- --strict
 3  Lint and format clean across every language present         make lint
 4  no-nondeterminism lint passes (no wall clock, no rand,      make lint-determinism
    no hash-map iteration order in output paths)
 5  Determinism: 3 identical runs, byte-identical artifacts     make determinism
 6  Rule-ordering property test (>=500 orderings) passes        make test-rule-order
 7  Demo path runs headless end to end                          make demo
 8  Vertical slice still alive                                  make demo-slice
 9  No TODO / FIXME / unimplemented!() / panic!("todo")         make grep-stubs
    / NotImplementedError on any demo-path file
10  No hardcoded results: no literal verdict, cut, hash or      make grep-hardcoded
    metric in source outside tests/fixtures
11  Every doc number traced to results/*.json                   make docs-check
12  Docs regenerated from code (rules, controls, status)        make docs-gen && git diff --exit-code
13  Certificate mutation suite: >=30 mutants all rejected       make test-mutants
14  Kernel vs concrete simulator, 256 configs per fixture       make gate-agreement
15  Go checker independence (no shared code/dep edge)           make gate-checker-independence
16  Haskell admissibility differential oracle agrees            make gate-haskell
17  Antitonicity over the control lattice                       make gate-antitone
18  Zero false ROBUST across the degradation matrix             make gate-invariant
19  Adversarial suite: suppression, backdating, duplication,    make test-adversarial
    reordering, corrupted chains, hostile rules file
20  Flags honoured: no flagged run renders ROBUST               make test-flags
21  No probability, confidence, cost-mass or invented dollar    make grep-forbidden-terms
    figure in any output or doc
22  LLM removal changes nothing but narration                   make demo NO_LLM=1
23  Resource caps enforced; grounding cap recorded not assumed  make test-caps
24  Assets newer than the code that generates them              make docs-check
```

56.2 Absolute prohibitions

- Do not write a test that asserts only `exit 0`, `is not None`, or `len(x) > 0` on a demo-path behaviour.
- Do not mark a test skipped to make a milestone green. Do not lower a threshold to make a gate pass. Do not delete a failing fixture.
- Do not commit a number to any document that you did not obtain by running code in that commit.
- Do not implement a stub that returns a plausible value. If a function is not implemented, it raises/panics and its caller is not on the demo path.
- Do not use an LLM anywhere in the reconstruction, liveness, grounding, cut, certificate or checker paths.
- Do not add a language by translating existing logic. Do not add a language directory without a test that fails under mutation.
- Do not claim ROBUST, minimality, soundness or prevention beyond the wording permitted in the ECLIPSE "may never claim" list.

56.3 Reporting protocol to the human

After every milestone, and whenever asked for status, report in exactly this shape:

```
MILESTONE M<n> — <GREEN | RED | PARTIAL>

WHAT RUNS
  <command>  ->  <one-line real output, copied, not paraphrased>
  ...

EVIDENCE
  anti-slop: 24/24 PASS        (or: 22/24, failing rows listed below)
  determinism: 3/3 identical   bundle blake3:<hash>
  gates: agreement 256/256, mutants 31/31 rejected, invariant 0/350 false ROBUST
  measured: grounding 2,104 instances; checker 11ms; ingest 418,220 events in 42s

WHAT I DID NOT BUILD
  <explicit list; never silently omitted>

WHAT IS STUBBED OR FAKED
  <file:line — what it returns — whether it is on the demo path>
  (If this list is non-empty and any entry is on the demo path, the milestone is RED.)

FLAGS ON THIS RUN
  grounding_capped | subset_minimal_only | greedy_cover | none

NEXT
  <the single next milestone and its first task>
```

Rules for reporting:

1. Show commands and their real output. Never describe output you did not produce.
2. Never say "should work", "is production ready", "fully verified", "proves the system is secure", or "detects attacks". Say what ran, on what data, with what result.
3. If you stubbed, mocked, hardcoded, shortened a loop, reduced a seed count, or skipped a gate to get something to run — say so in `WHAT IS STUBBED OR FAKED` in the same message, unprompted, with file and line.
4. If a gate fails and you cannot fix it, report RED with the failing assertion text and your diagnosis. Do not proceed to the next milestone.
5. Distinguish measured from expected. A number without a command that produced it must not appear.
6. When a design decision was forced, write the ADR before reporting.

56.4 How to begin

```
START HERE — do these in order, then stop and wait for confirmation.

1. Read the repository as it exists. Print the tree, the existing configs, and
   anything already present. Do not create files yet.
2. Read this entire prompt again end to end. List every requirement you believe
   is ambiguous or in conflict, with the section numbers. Ask about those, and
   only those.
3. Write docs/PLAN.md: the M0-M10 milestone list from section 52, restated in
   your own words, with per-milestone task breakdowns, the make targets you will
   create, the gates you will wire, and your estimate of what is risky.
   Include the language plan from section 19 mapped to M9.
4. Print the milestone list and the first three M0 tasks, and STOP. Wait for the
   human to confirm the milestone list before writing any code.
5. On confirmation, start at M0. Build only M0. Run `make anti-slop`. Report in
   the section 56.3 format. Do not touch M1 until M0 is GREEN.

Build the boring parts correctly first. The proof kernel is worthless on top of
an ingest path that is not deterministic.
```


# PART II — HARDENING ADDENDUM (SECTIONS 57-76)

Part II overrides Part I wherever they conflict.

============================================================
57. GLOSSARY, CANONICAL VOCABULARY AND ID TYPES
============================================================

This section is normative over every other section in Part I and Part II. It is the single authority binding each concept in SPECTRA to exactly one name, exactly one identifier type, exactly one owning section, and exactly one representation in each of Python, Rust, Go, TypeScript and SQL. Where any other section uses a different word for a concept named here, this section wins and the other section is wrong.

OVERRIDES Part I: Part I had no glossary. Terms collided across sections (`atom` meant both a ground fact and a control threshold literal; `event` meant both a real-world occurrence and a serialized log line; `adapter`, `parser`, `collector` and `shipper` were used interchangeably). Every such collision is resolved below and the losing term is banned from identifiers by `make lint-vocab`.

---

## 57.1 Rules of the vocabulary

1. **One concept, one name.** Every concept in Table A has exactly one canonical name. Every other word for it is a forbidden synonym (Table D) and is banned from identifiers in all source trees.
2. **One name, one type.** Every concept that has identity has exactly one identifier type with exactly one wire grammar (§57.2) and exactly one byte encoding (§57.3).
3. **One concept, one owner.** Every concept names exactly one owning section that defines its semantics. Owners are written as section numbers where already assigned, or as symbolic `PART-II/<slug>` tokens resolved through `docs/section-index.toml`. `make lint-vocab` fails on an unresolved owner.
4. **The table is machine-readable.** Tables A–D are generated from `docs/vocab.toml`. The markdown in this section is the rendered view; `vocab.toml` is the source of truth. `make lint-vocab` fails if the rendered view and `vocab.toml` disagree byte for byte.
5. **Same-commit rule.** Any commit that introduces a new concept — a new declared type, a new SQL domain, a new certificate field, a new enum variant of a closed set — MUST add its row to `vocab.toml` in that same commit. `make lint-vocab` enforces this (§57.10, check V8). There is no follow-up-PR exception.
6. **Closed sets are closed here.** `DimensionId`, `FlagId`, `OperatorId`, `OracleId`, the entity-kind enum, the `safety` enum and the `minimality` enum are closed. New members are added in this section or not at all.
7. **No bare strings in typed positions.** Every language binding is a distinct nominal or branded type. Passing a `RecordId` where a `FactHash` is expected must be a compile-time or lint-time error in Python, Rust, Go and TypeScript, and a domain violation in SQL.
8. **No aliases.** `type Ev = RecordId`, `using Fact = ...`, `pub use ... as ...` re-exports under a second name, and TypeScript `type X = Y` alias chains over vocabulary types are forbidden and are a lint failure.

---

## 57.2 Identifier grammar (ABNF)

All identifiers are US-ASCII. Lowercase only. No whitespace, no Unicode, no percent-encoding, no leading zeros in numeric fields.

```abnf
; ---------- primitives ----------
DIGIT       = %x30-39
HEXDIG      = DIGIT / %x61-66                  ; lowercase hex ONLY
lower       = %x61-7A
snake       = lower *( lower / DIGIT / "_" )   ; max 48 octets
u16         = "0" / ( %x31-39 *4DIGIT )        ; 0..65535
level       = "0" / ( %x31-39 [ DIGIT ] )      ; 0..99
h128        = 32HEXDIG                         ; run-local digests
h256        = 64HEXDIG                         ; integrity-critical digests
kind        = "user" / "host" / "process" / "session" / "credential"
            / "key" / "service" / "account" / "file" / "netflow"
            / "api_client" / "resource"

; ---------- integrity-critical (MAY appear in a certificate) ----------
record-id     = "rc:"   h256
bundle-id     = "bn:"   h256
fact-hash     = "fh:"   h256
instance-id   = "in:"   h256
license-id    = "lic:"  h256
cut-id        = "cut:"  h256
corridor-id   = "cor:"  h256
hypothesis-id = "hy:"   h256
hypergraph-id = "hg:"   h256
run-id        = "run:"  h256
cert-id       = "cert:" h256

; ---------- run-local (MUST NOT appear in a certificate) ----------
event-id      = "ev:"   h128
transition-id = "tr:"   h128
window-id     = "bw:"   h128
assignment-id = "asg:"  h128
degradation-id= "deg:"  h128

; ---------- symbolic (authored, human-written) ----------
source-id     = "src:"  snake
collector-id  = "col:"  snake "@" u16
control-id    = "ctl:"  snake
literal-id    = "lit:"  snake "@" level        ; snake = the control's snake, no "ctl:"
rule-id       = "rl:"   snake
state-id      = "st:"   snake ":" snake        ; dimension ":" state
dimension-id  = "dim:"  snake
flag-id       = "flag:" snake
scenario-id   = "sc:"   snake "@" u16          ; u16 = scenario schema version
operator-id   = "op:"   snake
oracle-id     = "orc:"  snake
```

OVERRIDES Part I section 10.2: `source_id` matching `^src-[a-z2-7]{16}$` and `collector_id` matching `^col-[a-z2-7]{16}$` — content-addressed base32 digests produced by section 12's resolver from the `src` and `col` entity kinds declared in section 9.2 — are replaced by the authored symbolic forms `src:` snake and `col:` snake `@` u16, which are never derived from a digest and are not entity kinds at all. An implementer following section 10.2 emits `src-`/`col-` base32 values that fail the `source_id` and `collector_id` grammars, invalidating both worked examples in section 10.7, and requires section 12's resolver to materialize two kinds that no longer exist.

OVERRIDES Part I section 10.2: `scenario_id` matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,63}$`, with the version held separately in section 23.2's `version` key, is replaced by `sc:` snake `@` u16, in which hyphens are illegal and the `@` suffix is the only place the scenario schema version is recorded. An implementer following section 10.2 emits `s07-token-pivot` or section 23.2's `sc_oauth_token_pivot`, both invalid here, and because section 9.3 anchors every `EntityId` on `scenario_id` every entity digest in every fixture is then computed over the wrong string.

OVERRIDES Part I section 13: the SCREAMING_SNAKE state names of section 13 (`AUTHENTICATED`, `EXFIL_STAGED`, `ELEVATED_JIT`), written bare, are replaced by lowercase `st:` `<dimension>` `:` `<state>` identifiers such as `st:session:active`. An implementer following section 13 generates Rust `enum` and Python `StrEnum` variant spellings that fail the case rule above, prints unprefixed names in section 15.4's mandatory CLI transcript, and stores states in section 15.2's `SMALLINT` columns rather than the `state_id` text domain.

Prefix uniqueness is a hard invariant: no prefix is a prefix of another prefix. `make lint-vocab` recomputes this from `vocab.toml` and fails on violation.

**Certificate width rule.** Any identifier matching an `h128` form appearing anywhere inside a certificate is a hard rejection by `spectra verify`, not a warning. Rationale: `h128` IDs derive from run-local structure and are never adversarially reachable; integrity-critical IDs derive in part from untrusted telemetry bytes, where 128 bits of truncated digest permits a birthday-grinding attack at roughly 2^64 work. Do not "optimize" certificate size by truncating these.

---

## 57.3 Byte encoding and canonical digest construction

1. Every digest is BLAKE3-256 over the domain-separated byte string:

```
DIGEST(kind, payload) = BLAKE3-256( "spectra/v1/" || kind || 0x1F || payload )
```

   `kind` is the ID prefix without the colon (`"rc"`, `"fh"`, `"in"`, ...), as ASCII. `0x1F` is the ASCII unit separator and may never appear inside `kind`.
2. An `h256` ID renders all 32 output octets as lowercase hex. An `h128` ID renders **the first 16 octets only**, lowercase hex. Truncation is a prefix, never a fold, never a XOR.
3. `payload` is the concept's canonical byte encoding, defined per concept in `vocab.toml` field `payload`. Canonical encodings are built only from: ASCII identifiers as written; unsigned integers as fixed-width big-endian (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`); and ordered sequences as `count:u32` big-endian followed by elements. **No JSON, no floats, no locale-sensitive formatting, no platform-endian writes, no length-prefixed UTF-8 with implementation-defined normalization.**
4. Sequences inside a payload are sorted by plain bytewise (`memcmp`) ascending order of the element's canonical bytes before hashing. Sorting is stable and total. Never sort by a language's default collation.

   OVERRIDES Part I sections 9.3, 10.2, 11.3, 14.1, 23.4 and 23.5: the five distinct digest recipes of Part I — base32 `BLAKE3_128` over LF/US-delimited anchor bytes, `BLAKE3_128` over RFC 8785 JCS JSON, `BLAKE3_256` over a `spectra.chain.v1` prefix with a little-endian `u64le(epoch)`, `blake3` over canonical JSON bodies, and a truncated `blake3(trace_root || seq || emit_index)` — are all replaced by the single `DIGEST(kind, payload)` construction of rule 1, whose domain prefix is `spectra/v1/` + `kind`, whose payload admits no JSON and no platform-endian write, and whose only permitted truncation is the h128 prefix of rule 2. An implementer following any Part I recipe produces a digest differing in domain prefix, payload encoding, byte order or width, so every golden hash, every `tests/golden/traces.json` entry and every committed certificate fixture changes value.
5. On the wire (JSONL bundles, certificate JSON, TOML catalogs, HTTP APIs) every identifier is the ASCII string of §57.2 — never a byte array, never base64, never an integer.
6. In SQL, every identifier is `text` constrained by a `DOMAIN`, never `bytea`, never `uuid`:

```sql
CREATE DOMAIN record_id   AS text CHECK (VALUE ~ '^rc:[0-9a-f]{64}$');
CREATE DOMAIN fact_hash   AS text CHECK (VALUE ~ '^fh:[0-9a-f]{64}$');
CREATE DOMAIN entity_id   AS text CHECK (VALUE ~ '^en:(user|host|process|session|credential|key|service|account|file|netflow|api_client|resource):[0-9a-f]{32}$');
CREATE DOMAIN literal_id  AS text CHECK (VALUE ~ '^lit:[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}@(0|[1-9][0-9]?)$');
CREATE DOMAIN tick        AS bigint CHECK (VALUE >= 0);
-- ... one DOMAIN per row of Table A that has an ID type.
```

   OVERRIDES Part I sections 9.2 and 9.3: the twenty-one-code entity-kind set (`idn, acct, svcacct, cred, sess, tok, dev, host, ctr, proc, svc, api, res, role, grant, netif, flow, zone, ctl, src, col`) and the wire form `EntityId := kind "-" b32` over lowercase base32 are replaced by the closed `EntityKind` set of Table C and the wire form `en:` `<kind>` `:` `<hex>` constrained by the `entity_id` domain above. An implementer following section 9.2 emits values shaped like `sess-k4m2q9x7t1b0dfe3`, which fail the `entity_id` domain on prefix, separator, alphabet and digest rendering and void section 10.2's `EntityRef` pattern, and builds resolvers for kinds that no longer exist (token, device, container, role, grant, zone, network interface, control instance, telemetry source, collector) while leaving `key`, `file` and `api_client` without an anchor tuple.

   OVERRIDES Part I sections 15.2 and 25.5: `event_id BYTEA`, `tid BYTEA`, `chain_hash BYTEA`, `run_id UUID`, `entity_id BIGINT`, `license_id BIGINT` and the `SMALLINT` columns for dimension, state, trigger, support and classification, together with `LicenseId(u32)` and `EventId(u64)` in code, are replaced by `text` columns constrained by the DOMAINs above and by the byte widths Table B declares, so `LicenseId` is a certifiable `lic:` h256 rather than a run-local integer and `RunId` is `run:` h256 rather than a UUID or section 10.2's `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`. An implementer following section 15.2 builds a schema in which every identifier column and every foreign key has the wrong type, and emits `run_id` values that fail the `run_id` domain on every canonical event and every fixture.

7. `Tick` is `u64`, an integer count of nanoseconds since the scenario epoch (tick 0). All intervals are half-open `[t0, t1)`. There is no floating point anywhere in the time model and no wall-clock value in any hashed payload.

   OVERRIDES Part I sections 14.4, 16.6 and 23.2: `tick = floor((t_norm_ns - run_origin_ns) / tick_width_ns)` with `tick_width_ns` configurable in `config/constants.toml`, and section 23.2's separate `tick_unit_s` simulator unit exported by section 23.8, are replaced by a tick fixed at one nanosecond; `tick_width_ns` and `tick_unit_s` cease to exist. An implementer following section 14.4 builds a quantized clock in which every TTL, idle and absolute expiry deadline, blind-window bound, `horizon_ticks`, `burst_window_ticks`, `snapshot_interval_ticks` and `min_reorg_horizon_ticks` is scaled by the old tick width, and one following section 11.4's closed gap interval `[a.observed_at_ns, b.observed_at_ns]` includes the upper bound, changing the SUPPRESSED licensing basis at that boundary.

   OVERRIDES Part I section 14.1: `wall_ns` as a required field of the transition record, hashed into `tid = blake3(canonical_json(record minus {tid, seq, superseded_by}))`, is replaced by a transition payload carrying no wall-clock value at all. An implementer following section 14.1's schema produces different `tid` values for two byte-identical runs on different machines, breaking the determinism guarantee asserted in section 15.6.

| hypothesis | `HypothesisId` | `struct HypothesisId([u8;32])` | `type HypothesisId string` | `HypothesisId` | table `hypothesis` |
| certificate | `CertId`, `Certificate` | `struct CertId`, `Certificate` | `type CertId string`, `Certificate` | `CertId`, `Certificate` | table `certificate` |
| verdict | `Verdict` (frozen dataclass) | `struct Verdict` | `type Verdict struct` | `interface Verdict` | composite type `verdict` |
| flag | `Flag(StrEnum)` | `enum Flag` | `type Flag string` + consts | `type Flag = union` | enum type `flag` |
| scenario | `ScenarioId` | `struct ScenarioId{name,ver}` | `type ScenarioId string` | `ScenarioId` | domain `scenario_id`; table `scenario` |
| degradation operator | `Operator(StrEnum)` | `enum Operator` | `type Operator string` | `type Operator = union` | enum type `operator` |
| degradation spec | `DegradationId`, `DegradationSpec` | `struct DegradationSpec` | `type DegradationSpec struct` | `DegradationSpec` | table `degradation_spec` |
| run manifest | `RunId`, `RunManifest` | `struct RunId`, `RunManifest` | `type RunManifest struct` | `RunManifest` | table `run_manifest` |
| oracle | `Oracle(StrEnum)` | `enum Oracle` | `type Oracle string` | `type Oracle = union` | enum type `oracle` |

Haskell, when the stretch admissibility oracle exists, binds the same names as Rust with `newtype` and is checked by the same lint; it is not a required column because the Haskell oracle may be descoped.

```

LivenessVerdict: LIVE BLIND SUPPRESSED                              (fail-closed = BLIND)
LicenseBasis   : BLIND SUPPRESSED OBLIGATION
Safety         : ROBUST OPTIMISTIC_ONLY UNSAFE
Minimality     : EXACT SUBSET UNVERIFIED
Operator       : delete delay duplicate reorder corrupt suppress    (exactly 6)
Oracle         : range_reexec go_checker generator_ground_truth
                 z3_test_only haskell_admissibility                 (exactly 5)
Flag           : grounding_capped corridor_capped subset_minimal_only
                 greedy_cover er_ambiguous liveness_uncalibrated
                 budget_exhausted realizability_unchecked
                 oracle_channel_absent quarantined_records_present
EntityKind     : user host process session credential key service
                 account file netflow api_client resource           (exactly 12)
```

OVERRIDES Part I sections 13.3, 13.5 and 14.1: the dimension enum `authentication, session, credential, privilege, device_trust, process, network_exposure, resource, service_identity, trust` is replaced by the closed `Dimension` set above, in which `authentication`, `device_trust`, `network_exposure` and `service_identity` are illegal `DimensionId`s and `identity`, `network` and `api` stand in their place. An implementer following section 13 generates FSMs, `st:` StateIds, coupling edges such as `service_identity -> credential` and `network -> device_trust`, a `dimension` SQL type and Rust/Python/Go/TypeScript enums keyed on names that are not members of the closed set; Part I defines no FSM, transition table or illegal-edge list for `api`, and that gap is owned by §13, not resolved by renaming.

OVERRIDES Part I section 10.2: the `Degradation.mutation` enum `["none","delayed","duplicated","reordered","corrupted","suppressed"]` is replaced by the closed `Operator` set above — bare verbs, no `none` member, `delete` added — each carrying an `op:` `OperatorId`. An implementer following section 10.2 emits past-participle values that fail the `Operator` domain, has no operator for `delete` and no `OperatorId` for `none`, and names the field `mutation`, which Table D bans as a synonym of degradation operator.

OVERRIDES Part I section 12.6: the certificate flag `ambiguous_entity` for a derivation whose leaves include an unresolved entity is replaced by `er_ambiguous` from the closed `Flag` set above. An implementer following section 12.6 emits an unknown flag that fails the closed-enum check in `spectra verify`, on exactly the runs section 12.6 says may not be presented as ROBUST without that flag shown.

OVERRIDES Part I / ECLIPSE §5: `Cert.mode: ROBUST|OPTIMISTIC` is deleted. A certificate carries independent `safety` and `minimality` fields plus a scope binding, because subset-minimality is a statement about cut size and has nothing to do with whether the goal is reachable. Collapsing them suppressed honest safety results for unrelated reasons and created an incentive to keep the control catalog small.

OVERRIDES Part I / ECLIPSE §8: a verdict is never rendered as a bare word. The only renderable form is

```
ROBUST(rules@<16hex>, catalog@<16hex>, licenses@<16hex>, non-adaptive) / minimality=SUBSET
```

No code path may build this string by concatenation; it is produced by one function per language, and `spectra verify` rejects any certificate whose verdict lacks a complete scope binding.

## 57.8 The three structural overrides that this vocabulary forces

**OVERRIDES Part I: `atom` is retired.** ECLIPSE §3's comment `FactId(u32) // ground, time-indexed atom` reads `// ground, time-indexed fact`. ECLIPSE §2's "atom set A" reads "literal set L". `Cert.cut: Vec<Atom>` reads `Vec<LiteralId>`. `goal.toml`'s "objective atom" reads "goal fact", and goals are a set with one verdict each.

**OVERRIDES Part I: evidence cites `RecordId`, never `EventId`.** `RuleInst.evidence: Vec<EventId>` becomes `Vec<RecordId>`, and every witness tree leaf is a `RecordId`. `EventId` is the generator's private identity for an occurrence; it is carried on the oracle channel, never in a bundle the kernel reads. This is what makes the zero-false-ROBUST invariant measurable under degradation: operators mutate records and therefore `RecordId`s, while `EventId`s survive, so §62 can re-link a perturbed bundle to ground truth through the `oracle_link(event_id, record_id)` table.

OVERRIDES Part I sections 10.2, 10.5 and 15.2: `event_id` content-addressed adapter-side as `evt-` + base32 of `BLAKE3_128(canonical_json_without_event_id)`, re-derived on schema migration by section 10.5 and redefined again in section 15.2 as a blake3-128 of the raw ingested bytes, is replaced by an `ev:` h128 minted by the generator when the occurrence is emitted, rendered as lowercase hex, and never recomputed from anything the kernel reads. An implementer following section 10.2 makes `EventId` a function of the possibly corrupted ingested bytes, so `oracle_link(event_id, record_id)` cannot re-link a perturbed bundle under the corrupt operator and the zero-false-ROBUST measurement silently stops working.

```
         GENERATOR                          KERNEL-VISIBLE                 ORACLE CHANNEL
         ---------                          --------------                 --------------
   occurrence --> EventId  ---------------------------------------------->  ev:9f1c...
        |                                                                       |
        +--> emitted lines --> [degradation ops] --> bundle.jsonl               | oracle_link
                                                         |                      |
                                                    rc:4b7e...  <---------------+
                                                         |
                          collector --> fact(fh:) --> rule instance(in:) --> hypergraph(hg:)
                                                         |                       |
                                          license(lic:) -+                   hypothesis(hy:)
                                                                                 |
                                                             corridor(cor:) --> cut(cut:) --> certificate(cert:)

   HARD RULE: no arrow crosses right-to-left from the oracle channel into the kernel path.
```

The kernel, the collectors, the grounder and `spectra verify` MUST NOT read the `event_id` field. A dedicated lint (`make lint-oracle-channel`, owned by §62) greps the kernel, collector and checker trees for `event_id` and fails on any hit outside the oracle crate. If `oracle_link` is absent for a run, the run sets `flag:oracle_channel_absent` and is excluded from every scored result.

**OVERRIDES Part I: threshold-literal bit positions are derived, not authored.** The 64-bit `blockers` mask assigns bit `i` to the `i`-th `LiteralId` in the total order: sort by `ControlId` bytewise ascending, then by `Level` ascending. Bit assignment is therefore a pure function of the control catalog, and a catalog edit renumbers bits. Consequently: masks are never compared across two different `catalog_hash` values, no mask is ever printed in a user-facing artifact, and every certificate records both the `catalog_hash` and the explicit ordered `Vec<LiteralId>` so that bit positions never need to be reconstructed by a reader. `make lint-vocab` recomputes `sum(m_k) + |controls|` and fails the build when it exceeds 64 (check V9).

## 57.10 `make lint-vocab`

One target. Deterministic, offline, no network, single-threaded, exit code 0 or 1. Runs on every push in the per-PR tier; it is cheap enough that there is no nightly-only excuse.

```
INPUTS: docs/vocab.toml, docs/section-index.toml, docs/vocab-allow.toml,
        all tracked files under services/ kernel/ checker/ frontend/ sql/
        collectors/ generator/ oracle/ docs/ README.md

V1  GRAMMAR        every prefix unique, no prefix is a prefix of another;
                   every regex in Table C compiles; every ID literal found in
                   fixtures/ and docs/ matches the grammar of its declared prefix.
V2  COMPLETENESS   every [[concept]] has: id_type|"-", owner, definition,
                   py, rs, go, ts, sql, and either forbidden=[...] non-empty
                   or forbidden_none=true with a written reason.
V3  OWNER          every owner resolves in section-index.toml to a real section.
V4  BINDINGS       for each concept and each of the five language trees, the
                   declared symbol is DEFINED exactly once (regex per language:
                   `class X`/`X = NewType`, `struct X`/`enum X`, `type X `,
                   `type X =`/`interface X`, `CREATE DOMAIN x`/`CREATE TABLE x`).
                   Zero definitions -> fail. Two or more -> fail (alias ban).
V5  SYNONYMS       tokenize every identifier in every tracked source file;
                   split camel/Pascal/snake/kebab/SCREAMING; match segment
                   n-grams against the forbidden list and the universal ban list;
                   report file:line:identifier:banned_term:canonical_replacement.
V6  RETIRED        any occurrence of a [[retired]] name as an identifier segment,
                   a JSON key, a TOML key, a SQL column, or an OpenAPI field.
                   No allowlist applies.
V7  UNREGISTERED   any identifier segment appearing in >= 2 of the five language
                   trees and >= 8 times total (illustrative, not a target) that is
                   neither in vocab.toml nor in vocab-allow.toml -> fail with
                   "unregistered concept: add a row to docs/vocab.toml".
V8  SAME-COMMIT    if the staged diff adds a `CREATE DOMAIN`, a new certificate
                   JSON key, a new closed-enum variant, or a new type matching a
                   vocabulary naming pattern, and docs/vocab.toml is unchanged in
                   the same commit -> fail.
V9  ATOM BUDGET    sum over controls.toml of (m_k + 1) minus |controls| <= 64.
V10 CERT WIDTH     no concept with certifiable=true has width h128; no h128
                   prefix appears in any committed certificate fixture.
V11 RENDER         regenerate Tables A-D from vocab.toml and diff against this
                   section's markdown; any byte difference fails.
```

`docs/vocab-allow.toml` entries are narrow and must justify themselves:

```toml
[[allow]]
term  = "message"
paths = ["frontend/src/i18n/**"]
reason = "UI string catalogue; 'message' here is a localized string, not a record."
```

An allow entry with an empty `reason`, or with a `paths` glob broader than one directory, fails V2. There is no repo-wide allow.

Expected output shape (illustrative, not a target):

```
$ make lint-vocab
vocab: 37 concepts, 1 retired, 28 ID types, 5 language trees
V1 grammar .......... ok      (28 prefixes, 0 collisions)
V2 completeness ..... ok
V3 owners ........... ok      (14 Part I, 9 Part II, 0 unresolved)
V4 bindings ......... FAIL
    concept 'corridor': no definition found in tree 'go'
      expected one of: type Corridor* / CorridorId in checker/internal/vocab/*.go
V5 synonyms ......... FAIL
    kernel/src/solve/cut.rs:114  ident `atom_mask`        banned `atom`      -> use `literal`
    services/api/routes/prove.py:88 ident `recommendation` banned `recommendation` -> use `cut`
    frontend/src/panels/Verdict.tsx:31 ident `confidence`  banned (universal) -> delete
V6 retired .......... FAIL    3 occurrences of retired term `atom`
V7 unregistered ..... ok
V8 same-commit ...... ok
V9 atom budget ...... ok      (61 of 64 threshold literals used)
V10 cert width ...... ok
V11 render .......... ok
lint-vocab: FAILED (3 checks, 5 findings)
```

CI binding: `lint-vocab` is a required check on every pull request and is listed in the milestone ratchet file. It may not be marked `continue-on-error`. A failing `lint-vocab` blocks merge with no waiver path; waivers exist only for `vocab-allow.toml` entries, which are themselves reviewed as part of the diff.

## 57.11 Negative requirements and forbidden claims

1. Do NOT introduce a second name for any concept in Table A, including "for readability", in a docstring, in a UI label, in an OpenAPI field, or in a commit message template.
2. Do NOT add a type alias, re-export, or wrapper that exposes a vocabulary type under a second name in any language.
3. Do NOT use `atom` for anything. It is retired, not deprecated.
4. Do NOT put an `EventId` in a bundle, a fact, a rule instance, a license, a witness tree or a certificate. Do NOT read `event_id` from any kernel, collector or checker code path.
5. Do NOT emit any field, column, JSON key, GraphQL field, metric name or UI label containing `score`, `confidence`, `probability`, `severity`, `risk`, `likelihood` or `priority`. There is no numeric grading anywhere in SPECTRA.

   OVERRIDES Part I section 16.5: the normative severity tuple `Sev(x) = (K, D, R, E)`, its `CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFO` band table, the `band=` query parameter on the findings endpoint, `dimension.criticality`'s stated purpose in section 13.2 and the mandatory severity doctest are deleted rather than renamed, because there is no grading concept for them to be renamed to. An implementer following section 16.5 ships a severity subsystem whose every identifier fails check V5, which §57.11.8 classifies as a correctness defect with no waiver path, so the work cannot merge.
6. Do NOT compare two `blockers` bitmasks, two bit positions, or two cut encodings across differing `catalog_hash` values, and do NOT display a raw bitmask to a user.
7. Do NOT render a verdict as a single word, and do NOT construct a verdict string by concatenation in any language.
8. Do NOT treat `make lint-vocab` findings as style. A synonym drift across two languages is a correctness defect, because the Rust kernel and the Go checker must agree on what they are checking.
9. Do NOT claim that this section makes the five implementations semantically equivalent. It makes them *nominally* aligned. Two components can agree on the word `license` and still disagree on when one is issued; that equivalence is the job of the differential fuzz gates, not of this table.
10. Do NOT claim a "shared type system" or "single source of truth for types" in README or docs. The honest claim is: one authored vocabulary file, five hand-written bindings, and a lint that fails when they drift or when a banned synonym appears.
11. Do NOT count the tokens in this section toward any language, format, or "concepts modeled" figure in the README. `vocab.toml` is configuration.

============================================================
58. DETERMINISM AND REPRODUCIBILITY CHARTER
============================================================

This section is a contract, not an aspiration. Part I asserted "byte-identical replay" in its
preamble and then left every mechanism that would produce it unowned. Part II makes it a
mechanism. Every requirement below states what "done" looks like and which gate proves it.

OVERRIDES Part I: wherever Part I permits a wall-clock timeout, a float, an unordered-collection
iteration, an ambient clock read, a locale-dependent comparison, or an unpinned thread count in
any path that can change a printed artifact, that permission is revoked. The rules here win.

Scope word used throughout: a **decision path** is any code path whose execution can change the
bytes of a hashed artifact — `liveness.json`, the fact base, the hypergraph, `Psi`, a cut, a
certificate, a run manifest, a golden fixture, or any number that reaches `docs/`. Everything
else (UI layout, log prettification, progress bars, plot rendering) is a **presentation path**.
Presentation paths may not feed values back into decision paths. There is no third category.


58.1 THE ONE CLOCK: TIMESTAMP TYPE AND WIDTH
------------------------------------------------------------

OVERRIDES Part I: sections 17-19 (temporal) and 25 (kernel) are hereby bound to a single time
type. Any Allen-interval or string-timestamp representation in those sections is a derived view,
never a stored or hashed value.

1. The one physical timestamp type is `i64` nanoseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, no leap
   seconds, no timezone field, no offset field. It is named `TsNanos` in every language:

   ```
   Rust:       #[repr(transparent)] pub struct TsNanos(pub i64);
   Go:         type TsNanos int64
   Python:     TsNanos = NewType("TsNanos", int)        # int, never float, never datetime
   TypeScript: type TsNanos = bigint;                    // never number
   Haskell:    newtype TsNanos = TsNanos Int64
   C:          typedef int64_t ts_nanos_t;
   SQL:        BIGINT NOT NULL                           -- never TIMESTAMP, never TIMESTAMPTZ
   ```

   OVERRIDES Part I section 2.4: "timestamps inside artifacts are scenario-relative, not
   wall-clock" is replaced by absolute nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, and Part I section 3.1's
   transition-schema field `"t": {"type":"integer","description":"scenario-relative microseconds"}`
   together with section 3.5's `interval: (Micros, Micros)` is replaced by `TsNanos`. An
   implementer who generates the Pydantic, Rust and TypeScript types from the section 3.1 schema
   as written emits scenario-relative microseconds, which no hashed artifact in this section
   accepts.

2. Forbidden as stored or hashed time representations: `float`/`double` seconds, `time.Time`,
   `datetime`, JS `number` milliseconds, `NUMERIC`, RFC 3339 strings, monotonic clock readings,
   and any value carrying a timezone. RFC 3339 exists only at the ingest boundary (parsed to
   `TsNanos` exactly, with a reject-on-loss rule) and at the presentation boundary (formatted
   from `TsNanos` with a pure function, always in UTC, always `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%9NZ`).

3. Representable range is clamped to `[0, 4102444800000000000)` (1970-01-01 to 2100-01-01).
   A record outside this range is quarantined with reason code `TS_OUT_OF_RANGE` per the
   ingestion section. It is never silently clamped, because a silent clamp manufactures a gap
   and therefore manufactures a license.

4. Durations are `i64` nanoseconds (`DurNanos`). Subtraction of `TsNanos` is checked; overflow
   is a hard error, never a wrap.

5. No component may read the system clock inside a decision path. The only permitted clock reads
   are: (a) the run manifest's `environment.started_at_wall`, which is excluded from every hash;
   (b) benchmark timers in the bench harness, which produce no input to any decision. A lint
   (58.6) fails the build on `SystemTime::now`, `time.Now`, `datetime.now`, `Date.now`,
   `getTimeOfDay`, `clock_gettime` outside an allowlisted file list committed at
   `tools/lint/clock-allowlist.txt`.

   OVERRIDES Part I section 17.1.2 and section 15.6: the three-clock record's `t_ing`, "the
   instant SPECTRA durably received the record", and section 15.6's permission for wall-clock
   reads at the ingest boundary are revoked for any value that reaches a hashed artifact. The two
   reads listed above are the only permitted ones and neither of them is `t_ing`. An implementer
   who populates `t_ing` from a host clock and lets that record feed `content_hash` makes the
   fact base host-dependent and trips the 58.6 lint.

6. `TZ=UTC` and `LC_ALL=C` are set in every Dockerfile, every CI job, every devcontainer and the
   `Makefile` itself (`export TZ := UTC`, `export LC_ALL := C`). A gate asserts both are set
   inside the toolchain image and that a run launched with `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` still produces the
